question.prompt: Each of \(2023\) balls is randomly placed into one of \(3\) bins. Which of the following is closest to the probability that each of the bins will contain an odd number of balls?

solutions.title: Add two balls at a time
solutions.explanation:
Adding two balls preserves the odd total, so we need to track only whether all three bins are odd or exactly one bin is odd.

Let \(p_k\) be the probability that all three bins are odd after \(2k+1\) balls. With just one ball, this is impossible, so \(p_0=0\). Consider the nine equally likely ordered choices of bins for the next two balls.

• If all three bins are odd, they remain all odd exactly when both new balls enter the same bin. Three of the nine choices work, giving probability \(1/3\).

• If exactly one bin is odd, all three become odd exactly when the new balls enter the two even bins, one in each. Either order works, giving probability \(2/9\).

These cases cover every possibility because an odd total requires either one or three odd bin counts. Therefore,
\[
p_{k+1}=\frac13p_k+\frac29(1-p_k)
=\frac19p_k+\frac29.
\]
To understand repeated applications of this rule, subtract \(1/4\):
\[
p_{k+1}-\frac14=\frac19\left(p_k-\frac14\right).
\]
Thus the difference from \(1/4\) is divided by \(9\) each time. Starting from \(p_0-1/4=-1/4\), we obtain
\[
p_k=\frac14-\frac{1}{4\cdot9^k}.
\]
Since \(2023=2(1011)+1\), the required probability is
\[
\frac14-\frac{1}{4\cdot9^{1011}}.
\]
It is slightly below \(1/4\), while every other listed choice is greater than \(1/4\). The closest choice is therefore \(\boxed{\frac14}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutions.title: Count odd bins across all assignments
solutions.explanation:
Because \(2023\) is odd, every assignment has either one or three odd bins. Counting how often a bin is odd will therefore reveal how many assignments have all three odd.

Track the bin chosen by each ball. There are \(N=3^{2023}\) equally likely assignments. Let \(T\) be the number in which all three bin counts are odd.

Count pairs consisting of an assignment and a selected bin whose count is odd. An assignment with one odd bin contributes one pair, and an assignment with three odd bins contributes three. Thus the total number of pairs is
\[
(N-T)+3T=N+2T.
\]
Now count those pairs by first selecting the bin. For a particular bin to contain exactly \(k\) balls, choose those balls in \(\binom{2023}{k}\) ways, then place every remaining ball into either of the other two bins. Hence the number of assignments where this bin is odd is
\[
O=\sum_{\substack{0\le k\le2023\\k\text{ odd}}}
\binom{2023}{k}2^{2023-k}.
\]
The binomial expansions of \((2+1)^{2023}\) and \((2-1)^{2023}\) have identical even-indexed terms and opposite odd-indexed terms. Subtracting therefore gives
\[
3^{2023}-1=2O,
\qquad O=\frac{N-1}{2}.
\]
There are three choices for the selected bin, so our second count is \(3(N-1)/2\). Equating the two counts,
\[
N+2T=\frac{3(N-1)}2,
\qquad T=\frac{N-3}{4}.
\]
The required probability is consequently
\[
\frac{T}{N}=\frac14-\frac{3}{4\cdot3^{2023}}.
\]
This is below \(1/4\), and all other choices exceed \(1/4\). Thus the closest choice is \(\boxed{\frac14}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
